sceneDescription: Inside an opulent, high-end retail showroom with velvet walls and platinum-trimmed display cases, a massive, hyper-polished vending machine stands center stage on a marble floor. Instead of snacks, the machine is stocked with luxury beauty products—serums, lipsticks, hair dryers, even a single antique engagement ring in a velvet box—each in their own softly lit compartment. The vending machine itself is crafted from rare woods and brushed gold, with crystal-clear glass panels. The absurdity: a white-gloved store attendant is carefully restocking the machine using silver tongs, treating each everyday beauty item as if it's priceless. In the background, a red carpet leads up to the machine, and a line of elegantly dressed mannequins (not people) waits behind a velvet rope, each holding a giant gold token. The lighting is refined and dramatic, reminiscent of a flagship luxury boutique, with gleaming reflections and rich textures throughout. The visual joke is the literal, absurd elevation of common e-commerce and beauty items to exclusive, rare-object status, referencing both the surge in online luxury sales and the exclusivity shakeup in the jewelry world.
